reference.source: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry / Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
clinicalPearls: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase-1 (CPT-1) is the rate-limiting enzyme of fatty acid oxidation; inhibited by malonyl-CoA during active lipogenesis
Beta-oxidation spiral four steps: oxidation (acyl-CoA dehydrogenase / FADH2), hydration, oxidation (hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase / NADH), thiolysis
MCAD deficiency: most common inborn error of beta-oxidation; presents with severe hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting, elevated octanoylcarnitine (C8)
Ketogenesis occurs exclusively in liver mitochondria via HMG-CoA synthase; produces acetoacetate, beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetone
Liver CANNOT utilize ketone bodies because it completely lacks beta-ketoacyl-CoA transferase (thiophorase)
reference.pathophysiology: Impaired beta-oxidation prevents gluconeogenesis during prolonged fasting because acetyl-CoA is required to allosterically activate pyruvate carboxylase. Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD) deficiency manifests in infants aged three to twenty-four months during intercurrent viral illness with lethargy, hypoketotic hypoglycemia, seizures and hepatic dysfunction mimicking Reye syndrome.
additionalInvestigations: Acylcarnitine profile by tandem mass spectrometry demonstrating prominent C8 octanoylcarnitine
Urine organic acid analysis showing dicarboxylic aciduria (adipic, suberic, sebacic acids)
Targeted genetic testing for ACADM c.985A>G mutation
